title: Normalize Game of Life cells before toroidal stepping
description: Repo-global public-invariant audit found that step_game_of_life_cells wraps generated neighbor coordinates but checks survival against the caller's unnormalized HashSet. An L-shape crossing the left seam therefore loses live cells with two neighbors, and extreme i32 coordinates can overflow in x +/- 1 before wrapping. Normalize and deduplicate input cells once at the shared step owner, preserve byte-identical behavior for existing in-bounds animation seeds, and add one seam regression covering the public toroidal contract.
close_reason: Normalized and deduplicated the live-cell set once inside step_game_of_life_cells before neighbor generation and survival lookup. The merged boundary regression failed on a seam-crossing L shape before the fix and now proves seam survival, zero dimensions, and i32 extreme safety. Existing in-bounds animation behavior remains unchanged. Formatting, debug/release tests, strict Clippy, examples, CLI help, render_once, timed Game of Life PTY playback, Cargo package verification, Nix path build, and diff checks pass.

title: Keep Game of Life dimensions inside its coordinate type
description: Game of Life stores cells as i32 coordinates but repeatedly casts public usize dimensions with as i32. Built public-API probes prove build_live_game_of_life_seed(20, i32::MAX, bloom) panics multiplying a wrapped dimension and step_game_of_life_cells({i32::MIN}, usize::MAX, 5) panics in rem_euclid. Add one saturating usize-to-i32 grid-dimension owner, pass representable dimensions through all seed builders, preserve every practical-dimension seed and step result, and extend the existing boundary regression check.
close_reason: Game of Life now converts usize grid dimensions once into its representable i32 coordinate space, eliminating repeated unchecked casts across seed placement and stepping. Practical dimensions preserve their arithmetic exactly; huge dimensions saturate instead of panicking, with the two-thirds placement widened through i64. Verified the formerly panicking public probes, the consolidated boundary test, 42 debug/release tests, Clippy, examples, Cargo package, Nix, and Matrix PTY.

title: Browse native Anima styles with previous and next keys
description:
## Why

Nova screen popup already launches Anima as `yzs random`, but Anima treats every key as exit. Choosing another visual therefore requires closing and reopening the popup or invoking a specific style from the CLI. Previous and next keys would turn the popup into a lightweight visual browser without adding a menu or configuration surface.

## Contract

Consumer: standalone `yzs` users and the Nova full-screen Anima popup.

Trigger: while a native animation is running, press unmodified `Left`, `h`, or `p` for previous; press unmodified `Right`, `l`, or `n` for next.

Result:
- Switch immediately to the adjacent native animation in one canonical ordered list and wrap at both ends.
- Rebuild the selected producer at the current terminal size without leaving and re-entering the alternate screen.
- Preserve the original overall `--duration-seconds` deadline across every switch; navigation never extends a Nova welcome or popup time box.
- Keep resize handling and frame cadence correct for the newly selected style.
- Preserve existing any-key exit behavior for every non-navigation key.

The initial style remains the explicitly requested style or the style selected by `random`.

## Scope

In scope:
- Browse every in-process `AnimationStyle`, including Boids variants, Game of Life variants, friends and enemies, Mandelbrot, and Matrix.
- Give the ordered browse list one owner and use typed animation styles rather than reparsing display strings.
- Extend the existing terminal input owner to distinguish previous, next, exit, and timeout.
- Document navigation keys in `yzs --help`.
- Keep direct `yzs STYLE` usage and the Nova popup path working with the same behavior.

Out of scope:
- Do not add a selector menu, HUD, persistent overlay, animation-name toast, keybinding configuration, history persistence, or shuffle state.
- Do not include `static`, `logo`, `random`, or the separately executed `asciiquarium` as browse entries.
- Do not change Nova popup policy or Zellij keybindings.
- Add no dependency.

## Implementation Notes

`screen_runner.rs` owns the animation session and already has the required style construction, per-style cadence, resize, input, and duration mechanisms. Keep switching in that loop. Replace the boolean keypress result with the smallest typed action that lets non-animation callers retain their current exit-on-key behavior.

The ordered browse list must be the sole navigation source of truth. A style change should render its first frame immediately, then use that styles cadence. A `random` launch may choose its initial dogfooded style as today and then browse the full native list.

Nova currently executes the packaged Anima binary directly for the screen popup, so downstream work should only publish the child revision, update the Nova Anima pin, and verify the real popup. No duplicate navigation logic belongs in Nova.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Focused tests prove every accepted key mapping, non-navigation exit behavior, previous and next wraparound, and stable canonical order.
- A deterministic session test proves switching rebuilds the correct producer without resetting the original duration deadline.
- A PTY smoke run injects both directions during a time-boxed `yzs random` session and confirms clean exit and terminal restoration.
- Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test`, `cargo check --examples`, `cargo run --bin yzs -- --help`, `cargo run --example render_once`, and `nix build .#yzs --no-link`.
- After publishing Anima and updating the Nova pin, verify the Nova screen popup can browse in both directions and still respects its configured duration.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if switching requires leaving the alternate screen or spawning one process per native style.
- Stop if navigation resets or extends the configured session duration.
- Stop before folding the external aquarium or card-like screens into the animation loop; that is a separate product decision.
- Stop if the design introduces a second style registry or a new dependency.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: crossterm already exposes the required key codes and modifiers. Expected package impact is a small Anima binary increase with no new store path or closure dependency.
notes:
Anima implementation complete; downstream Nova pin and popup verification remain.

Implemented:
- One typed eight-style browse order covers both Boids variants, friends/enemies, Mandelbrot, Matrix, and all three Game of Life variants.
- Unmodified Left/h/p and Right/l/n navigate with wraparound; other key presses exit.
- Press and repeat events navigate. Release events retain only the remaining frame wait, so enhanced-keyboard press/release pairs neither exit nor advance early.
- Style changes rebuild the producer at current terminal dimensions inside the existing alternate-screen loop and adopt the new cadence.
- One immutable timing value owns the original duration start and limit, so navigation cannot reset or extend the deadline.
- The input poller returns Option<InputAction>: absence represents timeout, while an exhaustive key matcher owns exit and navigation actions. Standard Option selection owns zero-wait non-key draining versus remaining-wait release handling.
- CLI help and README document the controls; no dependency or Nova policy change.

title: Emit terminal animation frames as synchronized updates
description:
## Contract

Consumer: every terminal receiving a full frame through `render_screen_frame`.

Trigger: static, logo, Boids, Matrix, Mandelbrot, or Game of Life rendering emits one complete screen frame.

Result: the ordinary clear, cursor moves, row clears, styles, and text are enclosed by exactly one `CSI ? 2026 h` / `CSI ? 2026 l` synchronized-output pair and flushed as one renderer-owned update. Unsupported terminals ignore the private mode and process the enclosed ANSI normally. Terminal I/O failure remains a bounded `io::Error`, and the end marker is still attempted after an enclosed write failure.

## Accepted implementation

`terminal_control::render_screen_frame` is the sole writer owner. It constructs the existing ordinary frame bytes, then uses the already installed crossterm 0.29.0 `SynchronizedUpdate::sync_update` implementation. Crossterm queues `BeginSynchronizedUpdate`, runs the enclosed write, executes `EndSynchronizedUpdate`, and flushes; the public renderer delegates directly to it. All styles continue through the same owner with no style branch, support detection, configuration, dependency, or public API addition.

The original 0.28.1 dependency note was stale after rebaseline; Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock resolve crossterm 0.29.0. Its exact registry source emits `ESC[?2026h` and `ESC[?2026l` and is MIT licensed. Ghostty documentation identifies unsynchronized large-screen redraws as a tearing source and directs applications to the synchronized-output protocol. The maintained contour-terminal protocol reference defines the same DEC mode 2026 begin/end semantics.

## Acceptance proof

One contract-first regression failed before the writer existed, then proved a multi-row frame larger than 8 KiB has exactly one begin prefix, exactly one end suffix, all content inside, and no newline-driven row wrapping. All 42 tests, strict all-target Clippy, rustfmt, examples, CLI help, `render_once`, git diff checks, and `nix build .#yzs --no-link` pass. title: Build a mathematical animation collection for Yazelix Screen
description:
## Why

`yzs` already proves that native terminal animation can make the Yazelix welcome surface distinctive, but its built-in collection is concentrated in boids, Game of Life, and Mandelbrot variants. A coherent mathematical-art collection would add visibly different motion families while preserving the standalone plain-terminal contract.

## Evidence

- `../yazelix-screen/src/screen_runner.rs` lists the current styles and owns CLI dispatch.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/lib.rs` exposes a foreground-only `ScreenCell`; `terminal_control.rs` has background styling only as a private output helper.
- `../yazelix-screen/Cargo.toml` currently needs only `crossterm`.
- Main Yazelix consumes the published `yzs` package through `flake.nix` and the `yazelixScreen` revision in `flake.lock`.
- FrankenTUI documents compact equations for Plasma, Gray-Scott, Clifford attractors, and radial wave interference at https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankentui.

## Scope

In scope:
- Deliver two enabling slices: reusable truecolor half-block field rendering and narrow scalar-density simulation helpers.
- Deliver native styles for multi-scale Turing patterns, primordial particle systems, Chladni cymatics, complex domain coloring, an attractor atlas, quasicrystal interference, Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion, Matrix rain, plasma, radial wave interference, Physarum trail networks, and later Lenia.
- Keep each effect independently selectable from `yzs`, bounded by the shared animation lifecycle, and usable outside Yazelix.
- Treat child publication and the main flake-pin update as an explicit integration boundary.

Out of scope:
- Do not migrate `yzs` to Ratatui, FrankenTUI, Kitty graphics, Sixel, or an image-backed renderer.
- Do not change main Yazelix welcome/session policy or make every new style part of the random pool without an explicit visual and performance decision.
- Do not combine all effects into one unreviewable implementation.
- Do not begin Lenia until the density-helper and Physarum slices provide real performance evidence.

## Implementation Notes

The half-block renderer blocks all dense field effects. Scalar-density helpers follow it and block Physarum and Lenia. Native Matrix rain is independent. Plasma and radial wave interference remain separate from quasicrystal plane waves. Land one effect at a time, reuse existing timing/input/resize ownership, and require a concrete dependency justification before adding crates.

## Verification

- Every completed child passes the standalone command floor in `../yazelix-screen/AGENTS.md`.
- Each exposed style renders nonblank deterministic test frames at small, normal, and resized dimensions without panics or stale cells.
- Each simulation has a representative frame-time or bounded-work check appropriate to its complexity.
- Published child revisions are pinned by main Yazelix before integrated runtime claims are closed.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop an effect if it requires host-terminal ownership, unbounded state, or a non-terminal graphics protocol.
- Split work further if a child cannot be reviewed and visually validated independently.
- Keep Lenia deferred if direct convolution cannot meet cadence after the shared helpers are proven.

## Maintenance Notes

Accepted after comparing formula-driven, fractal, artificial-life, and terminal-native candidates. Deferred alternatives include a general VFX framework migration, image-backed backgrounds, host-terminal shaders, and external aquarium/rain processes.

title: Generalize Yazelix Screen to render truecolor half-block fields
description:
## Why

Most proposed field effects need two independently colored vertical samples per terminal cell. The current `ScreenCell` stores one glyph and one foreground RGB color, forcing effect-specific packing and preventing a reusable truecolor field surface.

## Evidence

- `../yazelix-screen/src/lib.rs` defines `ScreenCell { glyph, color_x, color_y }` and the sparse `ScreenFrame` render closure.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/terminal_control.rs` already emits a foreground/background-styled glyph through a private helper.
- `../yazelix-screen/src/boids.rs` contains local half-block and background-tone logic that demonstrates both the visual value and the duplication risk.

## Scope

In scope:
- Extend the frame/cell contract so a cell can carry explicit foreground and background colors without effect-owned ANSI strings.
- Add a reusable dense field adapter that maps upper and lower RGB samples to `▀`, clips odd pixel heights, clears stale output, and reuses allocations across frames.
- Preserve ordinary single-color glyph rendering for existing styles.
- Define behavior for transparent/absent samples, zero-sized terminals, resizes, and color reset at row/frame boundaries.
- Add focused renderer tests and one small example or test fixture that makes visual inspection easy.

Out of scope:
- No Ratatui/FrankenTUI migration, image protocol, alpha compositing, sixel canvas, or general scene graph.
- Do not redesign every existing animation around the new adapter.
- Do not add a rendering crate unless measurement proves the current crossterm path insufficient.

## Implementation Notes

Keep terminal emission centralized in `terminal_control.rs`. Prefer a typed optional background on `ScreenCell` plus a field-to-frame adapter over preformatted escape sequences. Ensure Unicode width remains exactly one column.

## Verification

title: Add reusable scalar-density simulation helpers
description:
## Why

The half-block renderer converts finished samples into terminal cells, but particle trails and continuous cellular automata also need efficient scalar-field operations before color mapping. Implementing deposition, wrapped sampling, decay, and blur independently in Physarum and Lenia would duplicate the most error-prone numerical plumbing.

## Evidence

- The renderer foundation owns RGB sample emission, not simulation-field evolution.
- The Physarum particle model needs trail deposition, sensor sampling, diffusion, and decay.
- Lenia needs reusable wrapped scalar fields and bounded convolution over continuous cell values.
- Existing `../yazelix-screen/src/boids.rs` and `game_of_life.rs` each own specialized spatial state, with no general density-field helper.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add a small reusable contiguous scalar field with explicit width/height and allocation reuse.
- Support clear/fill, wrapped and clipped sampling, bounded additive deposition, decay, normalization, and one measured local blur/convolution path.
- Define resize behavior and prevent NaN/infinite values from entering palettes or terminal output.
- Provide adapters that let an effect map the scalar field through the half-block renderer without coupling simulation math to ANSI emission.

Out of scope:
- No generic tensor library, FFT framework, GPU path, arbitrary kernels API, scene graph, or replacement for effect-owned update equations.
- Do not force Gray-Scott or Turing patterns onto helpers that make their double-buffered update less clear.

## Implementation Notes

Keep the abstraction narrow and data-oriented. Prefer reusable scratch buffers and explicit boundary modes. Benchmark local blur before selecting a separable or summed-area implementation; do not add a numerical crate by default.

## Verification

- Tests cover indexing, wrapped/clipped edges, conservation for deposition before decay, blur symmetry, normalization, resize reset, finite-value defense, and buffer reuse.
- Benchmarks or timing tests establish a practical budget at representative 120x40 and 200x60 logical fields.
- Run the full standalone child command floor.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the abstraction starts encoding Physarum or Lenia rules directly.
- Stop and keep an effect-local implementation if a supposedly generic operation has only one real consumer or worsens clarity/performance.

## Maintenance Notes

This is the explicit later-stage prerequisite requested for density-heavy effects. It depends on the half-block renderer; Physarum and Lenia depend on this task.
design: Implement one normalized f32 field backed by contiguous reusable value and scratch buffers, exported from the existing crate root. Mutation inputs are clamped to [0,1]: NaN becomes zero, positive infinity saturates to one, and negative infinity saturates to zero. Deposit validates its external amount once, then saturates the sum with min(1.0) under the private finite-unit invariant. Internal normalization, blur, sampling, and palette mapping consume that invariant without duplicate sanitization. Keep boundary behavior explicit as clipped access and toroidal access. Provide only a wrapped 3x3 box blur and a mapper into the existing HalfBlockField. Do not expose Debug, Clone, or equality traits until a real consumer defines their semantics; scratch state is not logical field state. No generic kernels, boundary-policy abstraction, or dependency.
acceptance_criteria: A focused contract test covers clipped/wrapped indexing, bounded additive conservation, decay, normalization, blur symmetry and conservation, non-finite defense, resize reset, allocation reuse, and HalfBlockField mapping. Representative 120x80 and 200x120 pixel-field timings are recorded. The standalone Anima verification floor passes.
notes: Accepted state on 2026-08-24. One contract test covers clipped indexing, direct wrapped sampling, clipped saturated deposition and conservation, positive-infinity saturation from an empty cell, decay, nonzero and zero normalization, a corner impulse proving toroidal blur across both axes plus symmetry and conservation, NaN defense, resize reset, allocation identity across the blur buffer swap and resize, empty dimensions, and HalfBlockField mapping. Mutation-boundary validation solely owns the finite unit invariant: NaN maps to zero and infinities clamp to their respective endpoints; deposit validates the external amount once and uses min(1.0) for the already-finite sum. Speculative Debug, Clone, and PartialEq traits remain absent because scratch state is not logical field state and no consumer requires them. title: Add a plasma interference animation
description:
## Why

A classic plasma effect produces smooth psychedelic bands from a few moving sine fields. It is cheap, immediately animated, and visually distinct from cellular automata, particles, fractals, and radial wave interference.

## Evidence

## Scope

In scope:
- Combine a small curated set of spatial and radial sine terms over aspect-correct normalized coordinates.
- Animate phase and color cycling smoothly with bounded speed and no frame-wide flashes.
- Map the normalized field through a truecolor palette and add one `plasma` CLI style.
- Precompute frame-invariant coordinate terms and avoid per-cell allocation.

Out of scope:
- No shader runtime, arbitrary formula editor, audio reactivity, or direct FrankenTUI dependency.
- Do not merge this with radial `wave-interference`; they must retain different spatial structure.

## Implementation Notes

Expose the style through `ScreenStyle`, CLI parsing/help, and an explicit random-pool decision. Reuse the existing animation context for duration, input, resize, and terminal cleanup. Implement and verify in the child, push the child commit, then update only the `yazelixScreen` lock input in main Yazelix and verify the integrated `yzx anima` path.
Use FrankenTUI as a behavioral reference and implement the compact equation locally after checking provenance. Standard-library trigonometry should be sufficient.

- Visual fixtures confirm smooth bands, continuous color motion, and a nonblank frame at small, normal, and wide sizes.

title: Add a radial wave-interference animation
description:
## Why

Multiple moving wave sources create expanding, colliding ripple fronts and moire-like nodes. This is a separate visual family from quasicrystal plane waves and plasma color bands, and it can react naturally to terminal geometry.

## Scope

In scope:

- Correct distance for terminal aspect ratio and map signed interference to a stable truecolor palette.
- Keep source count and per-frame work bounded; precompute or reuse coordinate data where useful.
- Add one `wave-interference` CLI style.

Out of scope:
- No physical fluid solver, reflection/refraction model, interactive mouse sources, audio input, or arbitrary source editor.

## Why

A Physarum-inspired sensor-and-trail model forms branching transport networks, veins, loops, and pulsing fronts. It offers a denser and more structural artificial-life effect than boids or primordial particle clusters.

- Render trail intensity and fresh deposits through a restrained truecolor palette.
- Add one `physarum` CLI style.

title: Add a deferred Lenia continuous-life animation
description:
## Why

Lenia can produce smooth, mobile, organism-like structures unlike discrete Game of Life. It is visually compelling, but its continuous convolution and narrow viable parameter regions make it a later effect that should build on proven density helpers rather than forcing premature renderer abstractions.

## Evidence

- Bert Wang-Chak Chan defines Lenia as a continuous-space, continuous-time, continuous-state cellular automaton in https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.05433.
- The requested sequencing is explicit: implement Lenia only after the renderer and scalar-density helpers have proven efficient with earlier effects.

## Scope

In scope:
- Implement one documented Lenia rule family with a bounded radial kernel, continuous growth function, stable timestep, and a small set of known viable seeds/parameters.
- Use wrapped boundaries, reusable scalar fields, and the half-block renderer.
- Preserve recognizable localized structures through resize by deterministic restart rather than malformed resampling.
- Add one `lenia` CLI style only after the prerequisite helper contract is stable.

Out of scope:

title: Add a dense friends-and-enemies particle dance
description:
## Why

The documented friends-and-enemies particle rule produces vortices, tendrils, rings, and collapsing swarms from a very small O(n) update: every particle follows one friend, avoids one enemy, contracts slightly toward center, and occasionally rewires. This gives Yazelix Screen a dense generative particle field that is visually distinct from the current low-count sprite boids and from true Primordial Particle Systems.

The accepted visual direction is lots of tiny dots or blocks. The result must read as a dense swarm containing hundreds to roughly a thousand particles at common terminal sizes, never as a handful of large sprites.

## Evidence

- https://x.com/IsaacKing314/status/2086721066106253347 shows the desired high-density visual behavior.
- https://community.wolfram.com/groups/-/m/t/122095 documents Simon Woods original 1,000-particle rule, update equation, parameters, and rewiring rationale.
- `src/boids.rs:98-176` owns the existing 8-32-particle sprite animation and demonstrates the shared frame-producer lifecycle, but its visual identity and O(n²) neighborhood rule are intentionally different.
- `src/game_of_life.rs:83-94` defines `ScreenAnimationContext` and `ScreenFrameProducer`.
- `src/screen_runner.rs:11-35` and `src/screen_runner.rs:341-392` own style registration, construction, context, and cadence.
- `src/lib.rs:43-88` owns the current cell/frame surface.
- `yzs-mathematical-animation-collection-dou.1` already owns reusable truecolor half-block field rendering.

## Scope

In scope:
- Add one native `friends_and_enemies` CLI style implementing the documented simultaneous update:
  `p = 0.995p + 0.02 f(friend - p) - 0.01 f(enemy - p)`, with `f(d) = d / (0.01 + |d|)`.
- Give every particle deterministic initial position, friend index, and enemy index; occasionally rewire one particle using the same deterministic random stream.
- Use double-buffered positions so a frame does not depend on iteration order.
- Scale particle count with available half-block sample area while preserving a deliberately crowded result: at least 500 particles at 80x24 and at least 1,000 particles at 120x40.
- Render many tiny dots or blocks through the shared dense half-block field surface. Accumulate collisions as density or intensity instead of silently dropping most overlapping particles.
- Preserve terminal aspect ratio, bounded memory, deterministic resize restart, duration handling, any-key exit, and alternate-screen cleanup through existing owners.
- Add the style to parsing and help. Keep it out of the random pool until short-session visual dogfooding explicitly accepts it.

Out of scope:
- Do not replace, rename, or reinterpret the separate Primordial Particle Systems bead.
- No large directional sprites, social-network UI, graph visualization, user-editable relationships, particle-count CLI option, general particle framework, external process, GPU path, image protocol, or new dependency.
- Do not change integrated Yazelix welcome/session policy in this child issue.

## Implementation Notes

1. Add one focused animation module owning positions, friend/enemy indices, deterministic random state, rewiring, and reusable next-position storage.
2. Reuse `ScreenFrameProducer` and the dense half-block renderer; do not emit effect-owned ANSI.
3. Start from the documented coefficients and one curated deterministic seed. Add no tuning configuration until the default proves insufficient.
4. Rasterize point density into the half-block sample buffer with reused allocations. Prefer one restrained palette; velocity or density coloring is optional only if it materially improves legibility.
5. Register `friends_and_enemies` through the existing CLI construction and timing paths.
6. Record source provenance in a short source comment without copying Mathematica implementation structure.

## Verification

- Focused tests prove deterministic initialization and stepping, valid friend/enemy indices, simultaneous order-independent updates, finite positions, deterministic rewiring, resize restart, and the required 500/1,000 particle floors.
- A representative rendered-frame test proves collisions contribute density and the animation produces many occupied dot/block samples rather than large sprites or a sparse handful.
- Inspect deterministic frames at startup and after approximately 3, 10, and 30 seconds at narrow, 80x24, and 120x40 sizes.
- Measure a 120x40 frame with at least 1,000 particles and record whether it meets the selected frame cadence before changing the density floor.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo test`, `cargo check --examples`, `cargo run --bin yzs -- --help`, `cargo run --bin yzs -- friends_and_enemies --duration-seconds 3`, `cargo run --example render_once`, and `nix build .#yzs --no-link` must exit 0.
- Publish the child revision before any later main Yazelix pin update.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the shared half-block renderer is unavailable; do not bypass it with raw ANSI or effect-local foreground/background packing.
- Stop and measure before lowering the 500/1,000 particle floors or cadence.
- Stop if the result reads as another boids preset, requires large sprites, or loses the dense dots/blocks identity.
- Stop if faithful bounded behavior requires a new dependency or broader simulation framework.

## Maintenance Notes

Dependency decision: standard Rust math and the existing deterministic-random pattern are sufficient; add no crate. This is an O(n) directed-relation particle dance, not a local-neighborhood artificial-life claim. Review should prioritize density, short-session visual payoff, deterministic behavior, and clean terminal teardown.
notes: Accepted state pending commit/publish: friends_and_enemies is a deterministic O(n) half-block animation with 960 particles at 80x24 and a saturating 1,600-particle cap at 120x40 and extreme dimensions. One relations vector stores each particle friend/enemy pair; two initialization passes preserve the deterministic stream by drawing all friends before all enemies while removing one allocation and one length invariant. Particle count derives directly from half the terminal-cell area, and projection relies on bounds-checked float-to-index truncation. Rasterization clears its reused density and half-block buffers, then accumulates density and paints the final collision color in the same particle pass, avoiding a separate full sample-area scan. The private particle state remains finite by construction and bounded normalized updates, so projection does not repeat unreachable NaN/infinity guards for every particle; the 600-frame contract test retains the finite-state proof. The documented simultaneous coefficients are locked by an explicit stack-only equation/order test; the consolidated contract tests real 80x24 and resized 120x40 animation state, relation bounds, collisions, dense block output, long-run finite/dense state, deterministic rewiring, resize restart, and overflow capping. random.rs owns the shared size-derived seed and seeded-index mechanisms used by Boids, Matrix, and friends_and_enemies. Rewiring intentionally uses the terminal-cadence 75% gate but changes at most one particle per frame: testing the source roughly 10% gate collapsed this deterministic terminal seed to 42 occupied samples after 600 frames, below the accepted greater-than-150 density floor. The standalone play_style library example now parses, constructs, sizes, and paces friends_and_enemies, and its README command is documented; executing one bounded frame succeeds. The 80x24 ANSI capture remains byte-identical across core simplifications. cargo fmt, strict Clippy, 46 debug and release tests, examples, CLI help, render_once, a 3.014-second PTY run, and nix build pass. The module is 247 lines; the installed package remains 787,744 bytes with 8 closure paths and a 50,208,656-byte closure.

title: Replace weak Life presets with tumblers and retire bloom
description:
## Contract

## Evidence

- The current bloom uses R-pentominoes and an acorn, whose canonical 1,103- and 5,206-generation lifespans do not fit a short welcome animation.
- LifeWiki documents the Tumbler as a 16-cell, 9x7, period-14 oscillator with volatility 1: https://conwaylife.com/wiki/Tumbler

- Keep game_of_life_gliders unchanged.
- Replace game_of_life_oscillators with game_of_life_tumblers.
- Place bounded, collision-free Tumbler seeds appropriate to the logical grid size.
- Remove game_of_life_bloom and the old oscillator style from every public and random/browse surface.
- Add no engine, cadence, renderer, dependency, compatibility alias, or formula parser.

## Verification

- Representative narrow, normal, and wide seeds are nonblank, remain bounded, and render at exact dimensions.
- CLI help/resolution, native navigation, and balanced random-family selection expose only gliders and tumblers.
- The full Anima command floor and strict Clippy pass.

title: Add a multi-scale Turing pattern animation
description:
## Why

Multi-scale Turing patterns produce continuously reorganizing spots, stripes, membranes, and cellular forms from a compact local algorithm. They would be materially different from both Game of Life and Mandelbrot while fitting the existing finite grid model.

- Handle poles, zeros, overflow, and non-finite values explicitly rather than leaking invalid colors.
- Add one `domain-coloring` CLI style and select a restrained default function sequence.

Out of scope:
- No user-entered formula parser, symbolic algebra, arbitrary code evaluation, or exhaustive complex-function catalog.
